parsed.rationale: Both `HSBColor.uiColor` (line 53) and `HSBColor.nsColor` (line 63) live in the same file `Shared/ColorPalette/Sources/ColorPalette/HSBColor.swift` within the `ColorPalette` package and share a Jaccard similarity of 0.714, indicating the bulk of their implementation is identical. The only meaningful difference is the target platform type (`UIColor` vs `NSColor`). Extracting the shared HSB-component assembly into a private helper and delegating from both properties would eliminate the near-duplicate body while preserving the platform-specific public API surface. Neither property is test, codegen, mock, or sample-app code, so the duplication is a genuine maintenance liability.

specifics.proposed_action: Introduce a private helper method on `HSBColor` (e.g., `func makeColor(usingUIKit: Bool) -> AnyObject` or a shared `Color` value via SwiftUI/cross-platform abstraction) that encapsulates the shared HSB-to-color conversion logic, then have both `uiColor` and `nsColor` delegate to it. Alternatively, if the project targets both UIKit and AppKit, consider a `#if canImport(UIKit) / #if canImport(AppKit)` conditional compilation block that exposes a single `platformColor` computed property, eliminating the need for two near-identical properties entirely.
specifics.why_no_category_fits: The two members (`HSBColor.uiColor` at line 53 and `HSBColor.nsColor` at line 63) are computed properties on the same type in the same file, not separate types or protocols. The duplication is a platform-bridging pattern (UIKit vs AppKit) rather than a type-hierarchy or protocol-conformance concern, so none of the structured categories (extract-to-common, protocol-inheritance, default-implementation, pat-introduction, generic-parameterization, subclass-lift, macro-synthesis, composition, extension-consolidation) cleanly describe the fix. The right action is either a shared private helper or a conditional-compilation alias, which is a within-file refactor not captured by any schema.
